title: Baikal-HUNT calibrates optical modules for its neutrino telescope
excerpt: The Russian-Chinese Baikal-HUNT project began at the NEVOD complex of MEPhI the calibration of two submersible optical modules for the future neutrino telescope of up to 30 cubic kilometers in Lake Baikal, which will record neutrinos of more than 100 TeV.
content:
The Russian-Chinese Baikal-HUNT project has begun calibrating two submersible optical modules at the NEVOD complex at MEPhI. These modules are part of the future neutrino telescope of up to 30 cubic kilometers that will be installed at the bottom of Lake Baikal. The goal is to detect neutrinos with energies above 100 TeV as a continuation of Baikal-GVD.

HUNT strings and modules already operating underwater 🔬

The project plan envisions about 2,300 strings and 50,000 optical modules. Three strings and 24 HUNT modules have already been operating underwater since 2025. The current calibration will last six to seven months and will include weekly rotations of 15 degrees. This process seeks to unify measurement criteria in light of the discrepancies of tens of percent detected between Baikal-GVD and IceCube. The effort strengthens neutrino astronomy as large-scale scientific infrastructure.

Rotating modules 15 degrees per week, the new water sport 🏊

While some debate the tens of percent difference between Baikal-GVD and IceCube, the calibration team has found its routine: rotating modules 15 degrees every week for half a year. An activity that sounds like an aquatic choreography for particle physicists. Of course, if in the end the numbers still don't add up, there will always be the excuse that Lake Baikal has currents with minds of their own.
